text: Welcome to the Qualitative Coding Sandbox. You are the Lead Coder on a study of why students do, or do not, use the campus wellbeing service.
Your lead researcher is away for two weeks. Read the handoff, then open the shared project.
Documents are on the left and the transcript is in the middle. The panel on the right always shows your next step.
Start by segmenting. Highlight one complete idea, then choose Create quotation. The quotation appears in the margin.
Segment all six transcripts, then choose Finish segmenting.
Next, code. Select a quotation, choose Apply code, and type a code name, or reuse a code you already have.
The Codes tab holds your codebook. Drag codes onto the text, rename them, or merge codes that mean the same thing.
When you finish coding, the Codebook Confidence meter shows how well your codebook holds together.
A second coder read three transcripts differently. Classify each disagreement, and choose what to do about it.
In Gameplay 2, choose how many categories to aim for, then sort your codes into them.
Rank three candidate themes. Then a late transcript arrives. Test your top theme against it, honestly.
In Gameplay 3, build the interpretation map. Link each category to the theme, and back it with evidence.
Write a short memo for the Dean. If your analysis holds up, a peer reviewer will challenge it, and you answer with evidence.
The debrief shows how each decision shaped what you could see. There are no marks, just your evidence trail. You can watch this again from Help.
